pages.text: For many years, people moved from place to place to find food.
Then something important happened. People noticed seeds dropped on the ground began to grow.
Instead of searching for food, they began planting seeds on purpose.
They learned to grow crops like wheat and rice in different parts of the world.
Soon, people began caring for animals such as goats, sheep, and cows.
Animals provided milk, wool, and help with work. This is called domestication.
Because crops grew in one place, families began building homes nearby.
Villages formed as neighbors worked together to plant, harvest, and store food.
With steady food supplies, people could learn new skills like pottery and weaving.
Farming changed human history forever, allowing communities to grow and cities to begin.
